verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Steam rises from the pot she never measures anything in—

salt thrown like a question I keep meaning to ask

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a phone call unanswered, the ringing folded
into the drawer with spare buttons
and thread that matches nothing we own

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the missed calls stack like unopened mail—
somewhere a number still rings through
to a kitchen no longer there

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I dial it anyway some nights,
just to hear the dial tone hum
like her voice humming over the stove,
counting nothing, keeping time
motifs: a hummed tune over a stove

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the line goes dead but I stay listening—
static settling like flour dust
on a counter someone still wipes clean

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the cloth hangs damp on its hook again,
wrung out by hands not mine,
folding the silence into smaller squares

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I fold it smaller still, a shape
that fits inside my pocket—
proof I was standing in that room

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning finds the pocket empty,
cloth unfolded on the counter—
someone else has learned to wipe it clean

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I take the counter's shine at face value,
not asking whose hand made it—
some mornings the clean surface is enough

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the light moves on to someone else's kitchen,
leaves this one holding its breath—
I never learn the name of what I'm grateful for

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the breath goes out unnamed, unnoticed,
someone else will call it wind—
I sweep the floor and call it mine

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
dust settles where the sweeping stopped,
finds its own quiet name for staying—
the floor forgets whose hands made it bare

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
still I set the cup down soft
on wood that owes me nothing—
the shine again, and no one asking why

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning finds the cup still warm,
asks nothing of the hand that left it—
I answer anyway, in steam

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the window holds the light a while,
gives it back changed, without ceremony—
I take what's mine and call it borrowed
